title: Best tools, tips and tricks for a 2.5D game
author: Hobophilia
selftext:
Hey all, I am working on starting a 2.5D game, going with a similar pixel art like Ragnarok with 3D assets and making the characters 2D.

I’ve looked around but I am unsure on which tools are good to make customizable characters. I have tried pixellab to get proper references and looking at Meshy for the 3D assets but I thought it be best to ask people that have done this before so I don’t start completely from 0 again. I initially tried this when I was new with AI and it was…. A learning experience.

Right now my game is just browser based game but for the next step I want to go with this ragnarok theme.

I really appreciate any tips and tricks!

comments.author: altmanram
comments.body: It might be hard for AI to deliver good results to be fair with you.

comments.author: Mental_Tailor_4227
comments.body: I can’t even find a good 2d pixel art pixellab and spritelab never get it right

comments.author: Professional_Ask3718
comments.body:
Same as any game, go through your design doc with your ai first. Discuss how you want yiur game to feel, tell it you want it to be 3D levels with 2D sprites, and get an idea of the art style of both 3D and 2D elements.


Some people dont like the agent approach, but for me it made the quality so much better, so with all my projects i now run an art agent, a narrative agent, and a design agent that must all sign off on any art generated. They help build the prompts used to make the assets too. 


Art keeps the feel we are aiming for and makes them look like they belong in the same game. Narrative makes sure any art conforms with the story or background of a character. Design makes sure it fits with how the game plays. If something passes all three, it then gets to me for final sign off

comments.author: Extempes
comments.body:
I am using the following Pipeline: chatgpt > Autosprite > Claude for corrections, Lightning, Shadow and anything Else that makes the assets look better.

But tbh you need a good Art Direction, that helps you Set the tone, colors and themes youre going for. There is alot you should think about for Art direction what helped me alot was making a library with good and Bad exmaples/inspirations of a Style and what exactly was good one Bad ... There is probably more I dont think of right now.... Good luck ✌🏻
